background.text: The Virgin and Laughing Child, also called The Virgin with the laughing Child, or generally abbreviated as another of many depictions of the Virgin and Child, is a statuette originating in Florence and was made circa 1460. It is a terracotta figure of the Virgin Mary carrying the laughing child Jesus Christ. It has been attributed to Leonardo da Vinci as "the artist's only surviving sculpture". It was credited to the Renaissance artist and inventor by curators at a Florence exhibit in 2019, claiming that this was a student artwork submitted under da Vinci's master and teacher, Andrea del Verrocchio at age 19 or 20. It is currently on display at the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, where it has been since 1858.
